item.title: Pentagon grants DHS permission to test heat ray weapon for use at border
item.description:
📝 US officials had also considered deploying the system during moments of domestic unrest, including at the end of President Donald Trump’s first term when protests erupted over the murder of George Floyd, according to a former US official familiar with those discussions. Customs and Border Protection officials have previously entertained the idea of using the system in areas where there’s a high concentration of illegal crossings. Border officials have occasionally discussed potentially using the system as a crowd dispersal tool, but it has never been deployed.
🔗 Read more: https://www.cnn.com/2026/10/21/politics/heat-ray-weapon-dhs-pentagon

item.title: Is this the new cyber normal?
item.description:
📝 This happens so fast, in fact, that at this point I think it is a reasonable that the moment you announce a security patch should be taken as a last possible date that the full exploit is not being publicly or privately distributed. As LiveOverflow points out, LLMs make it very easy to create exploit slop that proves nothing and doesn’t work, but that doesn’t mean that the vulnerability isn’t real and easy to exploit using AI. You can have 10,000 bad slop exploits that don’t work but if there’s one that does, that’s all that matters.
🔗 Read more: https://drew.silcock.dev/blog/is-this-the-new-cyber-normal/
